status: Prototype firmware and wiring supplied; physical bench checks pending
architecture: One RP2040 Pico, the retained C1.1 dual-bridge PCB and two ADS1115 breakouts for four TPU cells

nail_bridges.wiring_note: Join the two S+ pads to each other and the two S- pads to each other on each full shear bridge, following the manufacturer's labeled pattern. Do not leave either half bridge disconnected.
nail_bridges.excitation: C1 board-side ratiometric reference; nominal 5 V through the checked filters and shunts

soft_cells.construction: Retained R1 CH2-CH5 pressure-film cells and conformal TPU saddles
soft_cells.circuit: 3V3 -> film in parallel with the remote 100k resistor -> ADC node -> specified pull-down -> GND
soft_cells.calibration_note: The reported conductance includes the continuity resistor. A physical resistor change requires new calibration.
soft_cells.reference_divider_resistors: Four measured 10k resistors, 1% or better, two separate dividers
soft_cells.acquisition: Both ADCs convert one input index concurrently. One index is serviced per bridge frame; every raw value carries its acquisition time.

controller.nail_interface: Retained C1 J1 pin map: clock GP16, serial clock GP17, data GP18/GP19, PDWN GP20, shunts GP21/GP22
controller.power: One Pico/USB source. All breakout power and I2C pullups use 3V3; C1 analog power alone uses the nominal 5 V feed.

required_checks: Both bridge excitation currents, startup electrical shunts and all bridge lead faults
All four TPU cells with resistor dummies, contact, release, open and short faults
Both grounded ADC inputs and both independent excitation dividers
Actual bus rise time, clock waveform, sample age, paired ADC timing and USB back-pressure
Physical force calibration, held-out contact locations, drift and moving-arm behavior
notes: This reuses completed readout hardware to isolate the new nail mechanics. It is not a claim of a fully consolidated production readout.
Pressure channels update more slowly than the two nail bridges; retained timestamps must be used when comparing latency or dynamic data.
No physical readout, force calibration or completed N1 prototype is represented by this file.
